evidence: Cic. Lael. 98: semper auget assentātor id, quod is, cujus ad voluntātem loquitur, vult esse magnum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The man who agrees with everything; Cicero’s usual word.

evidence: Auct. Her. 4.21: nōlō esse laudātor, nē videar adūlātor (Lewis & Short)

terms.comment: Formed on adūlātor; not in Lewis & Short.

sources: Lewis & Short: assentator · Lewis & Short: adulator
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 272.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
